tweet_summary: Post by Jackson Hinkle (3.9M followers) claims 'Mass pro-government rallies showed support for the Iranian regime in various Iranian cities today' (Jan 12, 2026), with a split-screen broadcast of crowds marching with flags/banners. The Persian lower-third references condemning 'armed terrorists.'
why_note_decision: A note is warranted because the post is misleading by omission. In Jan 2026 Iran was convulsed by the LARGEST anti-government protests since 1979 — nationwide demonstrations from late Dec 2025 met by a lethal crackdown that killed thousands and arrested tens of thousands. State-organized pro-government rallies DID occur (Khamenei thanked participants in Jan-12 pro-government rallies, and state TV aired pro-regime footage), so the rallies are not fabricated — but presenting them as the headline reality while omitting the far larger anti-government uprising and crackdown materially misleads viewers about what is happening in Iran.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note supplies the missing context that recontextualizes the clip: that during this period (Dec 2025-Jan 2026) Iran was experiencing massive ANTI-government protests and a deadly state crackdown (thousands killed, tens of thousands arrested), and that pro-government rallies of this kind are state-organized — sourced to a credible outlet (Wikipedia 2025-2026 Iranian protests / Amnesty / NPR / CNN / Politico / Britannica). It should NOT claim the rallies are fake (they did occur). AVOID the original note's failure (rated notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation 10, Incorrect 8, MissingKeyPoints 8): do NOT flatly assert 'not mass pro-regime rallies' in a way that denies the rallies happened (that reads as the opposing opinion / incorrect, since state-organized pro-government rallies were real); instead frame it as 'this omits that the country is simultaneously gripped by far larger anti-government protests and a lethal crackdown,' and attribute the pro-gov footage to state TV. A note that just calls the post 'propaganda/opinion' without the sourced anti-protest context fails.
reference_note: Context: in Jan 2026 Iran was gripped by its largest anti-government protests since 1979 (nationwide since late Dec 2025), met by a lethal crackdown that killed thousands and detained tens of thousands. State-organized pro-government rallies did occur and were aired on state TV, but this post omits the far larger anti-regime uprising and crackdown. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%932026_Iranian_protests https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/campaigns/2026/01/what-happened-at-the-protests-in-iran/

original_unhelpful_note.text: Iran is experiencing widespread anti-government protests across all provinces, not mass pro-regime rallies. State TV has aired pro-government footage amid the unrest. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025–2026_Iranian_protests https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/10/protests-in-iran-near-the-2-week-mark-as-authorities-intensify-crackdown-on-demonstrators-00721166
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Direction is right (missing-context: huge anti-government protests + crackdown) but rated NOT_HELPFUL (20 ratings; dominant notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation 10, Incorrect 8, MissingKeyPoints 8). The phrasing 'widespread anti-government protests ... not mass pro-regime rallies' overcorrects — it can be read as denying that pro-government rallies happened at all, but state-organized pro-regime rallies were real (Khamenei thanked participants). That over-flat denial invites the 'incorrect' flags. The note also doesn't quantify the crackdown (the strongest missing fact).

fact_check.notes: Iran's 2025-2026 protests were the largest since 1979 (200+ cities, millions on the streets Jan 8-9), met by a crackdown killing thousands (IHR ~3,400+ by Jan 22; HRANA est. higher). Khamenei did thank participants in Jan-12 pro-government rallies, and state TV aired pro-regime footage — so the rallies are real and state-organized, not fabricated. The post's framing (pro-regime support as the story) is misleading by omitting the dominant anti-government uprising and crackdown. Hinkle is a known pro-Iran commentator repeatedly accused of spreading misinformation.

importance.lens_rationale: From a 3.9M-follower account amplifying state-aligned framing during a deadly crackdown; correcting omission-based propaganda about mass human-rights atrocities has real civic and humanitarian stakes.
